headline: Oil Declines on Signs of Moves Toward Gulf War De-Escalation
author: Charles Gorrivan

paragraphs.text: Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:38 AM CST 1 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Oil erased an earlier advance as traders weighed reports of US engagement in efforts to step up negotiations in the Middle East.

Global benchmark Brent traded below $98 a barrel after climbing almost 4% higher in the previous session, extending a volatile stretch in which prices have swung within a $19 range since Monday. Qatar Emir Sheikh Tamim Bin Hamad Al-Thani discussed diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region with US President Donald Trump during a phone call, according to the Emir's office.

Hopes are rising for a quicker resolution to the conflict, but major differences remain. Iran wants a US naval blockade lifted, sanctions eased and frozen assets released before fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The New York Times reported that Tehran is reviewing mediator proposals on its nuclear program, suggesting Qatar's efforts to avert renewed full-scale conflict are gaining traction.
Brent had gained as much as 2.6% earlier on Friday. US benchmark WTI also erased an advance to trade around $90 a barrel.
